searchText: Thanks for reporting, does this fix it? https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/pull/89/commits/9a40aaaa9936c7bf89774e1722663f1894c30530 It does explain it a bit more, next question :D > execute the container in "initcode-mode" and deduct gas for execution Does this mean we give the initcode a stipend of all available gas or are we still doing the 63/64 rule? The 63/64 rules is kept unchanged. Is EIP150 applied before or after the hashing charge? (after would be consistent with the other create instructions) Generally this follows CREATE2 workflow. Are we still checking MaxInitCodeSize? EIP150 or EIP170 (max code size)? 150 well both I see that 170 is applied after deploying? Re EIP170/3860 the answer is - max code size is checked in EOFCREATE flow spec (same applies to TXCREATE): "if updated deploy container size exceeds `MAX_CODE_SIZE` instruction exceptionally aborts". After hshing charge, just before deploying - max initcode size is checked as part of transaction validation (for InitcodeTransactions) And if by EIP150 you mean the 63/64 rule, after hashing Is there any tool to dump a testnet/mainnet transaction? E.g. generate a state test file with prestate and the given transaction? Next question: in order to check which initcode to use, I need to hash all initcodes of a transaction, right? Are these costs reflected in the opcode or is the implementation supposed to hash them before calling into the evm? What happens if the initcodes array contains an empty element and we query it with keccak([]byte{})? Should we start the creation process regardless or do we return 0 on the stack same as if the initcode was not found <@393119312350543872> added a script to create a blockchain test EEST filler (python): https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/3a6520e9411748ef33e6d072d639c6bea70998d6/src/cli/gentest.py Correct. (for others reading - this applies to InitcodeTransaction and TXCREATE being used in EOF) Not sure about the latter part (when hash). Re the cost, charging extra for all `initcodes` was considered, but I think dropped from the design, because the calldata cost charged is much higher anyway empty elements are invalid under tx validation rules ("invalid if (...) any entry in initcodes has zero length"). This is a more recent addition, not yet merged into the EIP, only in the Megaspec doc how can i change my http cors to global, from local host ? This is nice. Can someone actually dump some transactions for me? What are the rules for the immediates for dupN, swapN regarding overflows of the immediate? Can someone point me to the eip for the exchange instruction, seems a bit unnecessary to me https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-663 runtime overflow? we read an 8bit immediate and add 1 to it, should that overflow, or do we cast it to a bigger type before adding 1 you should use bigger type to get 256. Exchange was an explicit request from a compiler team. Why not make exchange take two immediates and get rid of swapN? One less byte. A code analysis seemed to show 17 and limited acces to 32 covers 80% Here's a quick document summarizing my opinions on the relative importance of each EOF feature. Spoiler alert: it's top heavy. https://hackmd.io/@shemnon/mega-eof-scoping The EOF call has knelt to the power of Daylight Saving Time and moved their weekly call back an hour to 1500GMT Wednesday (tomorrow/today). If you have burning questions about EOF (such as Prague scope, tweaking specs, etc) this is the right call to be on. https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1014 <@543900561460822016> is this branch the latest on 3074? Besu is starting to hack at 3074 impl. and were looking for reference code / interop testing https://github.com/lightclient/go-ethereum/tree/eip-3074 yeah sorry that is the latest, i haven't updated it yet to have the nonce no problem - I'll follow there for updates. let me know if that changes

excerpts.author: pdobacz

Re EIP170/3860 the answer is
- max code size is checked in EOFCREATE flow spec (same applies to TXCREATE): "if updated deploy container size exceeds `MAX_CODE_SIZE` instruction exceptionally aborts". After hshing charge, just before deploying
- max initcode size is checked as part of transaction validation (for InitcodeTransactions)
